subject: mirt, multipleGroup: M2 statistics cannot compute with missing data

messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: mirt, multipleGroup: M2 statistics cannot compute with missing data
parts:
Hi all,

I was using multipleGroup in mirt. My data contains 20 items with some missing data, i.e. for one response, I might have few items missing within all 20 items. I am able to run the following codes without any error and the corresponding ANOVA test (see codes below). However, in addition to ANOVA (because I feel like p-values are highly sensitive to sample size), so I would like to also compare the M2() statistics for the measurement invariance (e.g. comparing the difference of CFI between 2 nested models). 

Codes that worked: 


mod_configural <- multipleGroup (data, models, group = group)
mod_mertic <- multipleGroup (data, models, group = group3, invariance=c('slopes'))
anova(mod_metric, mod_configural)



Codes that did not work:

M2(mod_metric)
M2(mod_configural)


Error: Fit statistics cannot be computed when there are missing data. Pass a suitable impute argument to compute statistics following multiple data imputations. 

Any though help me out of this would be very much appreciated! 

Thanks in advance,
Yingyi

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirt, multipleGroup: M2 statistics cannot compute with missing data
parts:
You can either impute the data via the inputs to M2(), or create subset objects which remove the missing data but still retain the ML parameter estimates. This has been discussed on the forum as well, so you should be able to track it down fairly quickly. Missing data is a design problem, so dealing with these values takes a bit of thought, and depending on the statistics being investigated there may be different optimal strategies (e.g., the Q3 itemfit statistics are well defined with missing data, but S-X2 is not, nor is M2). 

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirt, multipleGroup: M2 statistics cannot compute with missing data
parts:
Of note, if you are willing to install the development version on Github I've added a new na.rm logical flag to remove the missing data row-wise in itemfit(), M2(), and fscores(). That should save a bit of hacking in the future.

Phil
